text:
maya: FYI we're seeing a sustained provisioning backlog in us-west1 for the last ~30m. GPUs are queued but kernels stay Pending. quick root look shows local NVMe scrub processes pegging IOPS on a subset of hosts.

ryan: ugh. any scrub logs or iostat?

maya: pasted quick snippets below (host gnode-uw1-103):

```
$ iostat -x 1 5
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  rrqm/s  wrqm/s r_await w_await aqu-sz  %util
nvme0n1         120.00 2500.00  1024.0  81920.0    0.00    0.00   0.40  12.50   5.00  98.50
nvme1n1          10.00  300.00    64.0   9216.0    0.00    0.00   0.20   6.10   0.50  45.20
```

and scrub log excerpt: 
```
2026-03-20T13:02:11Z scrubber[4721]: start batch 24 parallel=48 target=full
2026-03-20T13:02:12Z scrubber[4721]: worker 12: read 1.2G, write 0.9G, errors=0
2026-03-20T13:02:15Z scrubber[4721]: throttling not applied (rate=unlimited)
```

maya: scrubber parallelism jumped after last scrub-release. looks like a config default changed from 8->48.

ops-bot: ALERT: nvme_util_high on cluster us-west1. Link: https://internal/alerts/ALRT-6732 :warning:

sophia: if that's the case we should throttle scrubber immediately. option: set SCRUB_PARALLELISM=8 via runtime flag for the janitor service. we can do a per-node rate limit too.

alan: confirmed — deployment 2026-03-20T12:50 bumped default parallelism in scrubber config (PR #5123). didn't gate by node class. my bad.

ryan: mitigation plan? pause scrub on hosts with GPU-attach backlog, or throttle globally?

maya: temporary mitigation I suggest: 1) add node label scrub-paused=true to hot nodes (k8s), 2) instruct janitor to skip labeled nodes, 3) revert config in scrubber deploy to previous default, 4) drain backlog by restarting attach queue.

alan: i'll roll a quick hotfix to set default back to 8 and push a flag to honor node labels. prepping rollback now.

deploy-bot: Started rollout scrubber-v2.4.1-hotfix -> canary (5 pods)

maya: applying node label to top 12 hosts now. command: `kubectl label node gnode-uw1-{090..101} scrub-paused=true`

sophia: also recommend enabling token-bucket throttling on scrubber: `--max-io=100MB/s --burst=40MB` in addition to parallelism cap. reduces read storms.

alan: rollback complete, canary looks good. scrub parallelism back to 8. deploy-bot shows success on canary.

deploy-bot: Rollout scrubber-v2.4.1-hotfix -> 20% complete, no unhealthy pods detected.

ryan: after label + rollback we saw attach queue drop from 230 -> 12 in ~7m on sampled hosts. :thumbsup:

maya: confirmed GPU provisioning resumed for pending pods. still want to keep scrub paused on extremely hot hosts for next 2h while we monitor.

alan: logging ticket for follow-up: need safer defaults + config validation in CI to prevent accidental parallelism explosions. PR to add an assert in startup that parallelism <= 16 unless env AUTHORIZED_HIGH_SCRUB set.

maya: creating infra ticket and postmortem stub. also add an alert refinement: separate scrub_iops vs general nvme_util so we don't auto-blame normal GC jobs.

sophia: agree, and add a runbook step so on-call can throttle scrub via configmap rather than labeling nodes as a last resort.

maya: thanks all. will update the ticket with host list and timeline. leaving scrub paused on labeled nodes for 2h, monitoring dashboards now (watching nvme %util and attach_latency).

alan: sorry for the churn — will add a blameless postmortem entry.

maya: closing channel for now, will ping if anything regress. :eyes:
